identification: Keen's Genuine Tasmanian Curry Powder 4 oz canister, cylindrical tin (grey metal push-on lid and base rim) wrapped in a dark blue paper label printed in gold: 'Keen's Genuine Tasmanian Curry Powder, manufactured at Kingston, Browns River', central roundel of the 1866-7 Intercolonial Exhibition (Melbourne) medal 'Medal awarded to J Keen', jurors' report text, 'Manufactured by Keen's Curry Powder Co.', '4 OZS. NETT' on the seam, recipe panels on the back mentioning Keen's Tasmanian Sauce. H 8 cm. Imperial weight and the Tasmanian maker name (no Reckitt & Colman credit) point to the Watson-family era, roughly 1915 to 1954, before the formula and rights were sold to Reckitt & Colman in 1954. Condition: label scuffed with a tear/lift along the top edge and corner, rust on the base rim, contents unknown.

viewing_check: Check the label is original (not a modern reproduction wrap): look for genuine age toning under the gold, glue staining, and that the tin body under the torn top edge is old tinplate. Check base and lid for any maker or 'Reckitt' stamping. Check lid fits and whether powder is inside.
